info.name: Privilege MCP Simple (BFF relay)
info.description:
Exercises /api/privilege-mcp-simple — the minimal Privilege-style path: client_credentials token in, MCP JSON-RPC out.

The BFF does the hard parts for you: it mints the token, attaches the mTLS client certificate when MCP_MTLS_ON is set, runs the initialize / notifications-initialized handshake, and adds mcp-protocol-version to every later call. So these requests are plain JSON over HTTPS with no auth header of your own.

SETUP: Postman must trust the demo's local certificates. Settings > General > 'SSL certificate verification' OFF, or add the mkcert root CA.

The 'Direct token (what the BFF does)' folder is educational — it mints the same token yourself so you can decode it and see aud=mcpserver.ping.demo.

request.description:
Mints the token if needed, runs the MCP handshake, returns the real tool catalogue from the MCP server.

Saves the first tool name to {{first_tool}} for the next request.

exec: // count:0 is CORRECT here: a client_credentials token is a machine
// identity with no user, so it owns no accounts. Non-empty data needs
// the interactive route (/api/privilege-mcp), which carries a user.

request.description:
Invoke one tool by name.

Expect result.content with isError:false. count:0 is correct — the machine token has no user, so it owns no accounts.

The exact token request the relay makes.

TWO THINGS MATTER:

1. scope MUST be named. A bare client_credentials on this app is rejected: 'May not request scopes for multiple resources' — the app holds grants on three resources and PingOne will not guess.

2. 'mcp:invoke' alone is not enough. It opens the transport but every tool then fails with 'Insufficient scope for tool ...' — the per-tool check wants the data scopes too. Hence 'read write mcp:invoke', all on the mcpserver.ping.demo resource.

Straight at the MCP server, bypassing the BFF.

EXPECT THIS TO FAIL FROM POSTMAN when mTLS is on: the server requires a client certificate whose SHA-256 matches the gateway's, and it is reachable only on the Docker network (mcp-server:8080). Add certs/gw-mtls/gw-client.crt + .key in Postman Settings > Certificates if you want to try it, and run Postman where that host resolves.

The point of this request is to show what the BFF relay absorbs for you.
